BENECON312.name: Econometrics

Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

options.label: Mathematics, econometrics and optimisation
options.labelReason: Mathematics, statistics and economics support econometric modelling, while algorithms, linear programming and AI decision methods address optimisation. These courses make up a quantitative composition with substantive operations-research overlap.
options.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, probability and econometrics to analyse economic data. Study linear programming, graph algorithms and decision-making under uncertainty to model how systems can work more efficiently.
progression: Programming precedes algorithms and advanced AI. Mathematical Methods precedes Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics and later mathematical study. Data Science precedes machine learning, and statistics precedes econometrics.

options.label: Econometrics, finance and market analysis
options.labelReason: Econometrics and quantitative methods support a coherent applied option in financial markets, consumer behaviour and market research. Finance and market research receive more weight than mathematical optimisation.
options.concept: Use statistics, econometrics and computing to study financial and market questions. Combine banking and asset pricing with consumer behaviour and practical market research to understand how firms and investors make decisions.
options.distinctness: Seven courses differ in each direction. This option adds finance, marketing, market research, public economics, business AI, business foundations and databases. The closest option gives those places to advanced calculus, numerical methods, logic, algorithms and optimisation.
progression: Business foundations precede market research and finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics and deep learning. Introductory data handling precedes machine learning, and statistics precedes econometrics.

analysis: The closest option connects single- and multivariable calculus, linear algebra, probability, inference and regression to economic applications. Its discrete mathematics develops proof and formal reasoning while Advanced Calculus focuses on applied multivariable work. Optimisation includes linear programming, constraint satisfaction and discrete and continuous methods. Algorithms & Data Structures covers graph traversal, shortest paths and minimum spanning trees, providing direct operations-research overlap. Advanced Algorithms adds algorithmic arithmetic and complexity. Bayesian decision-making and reinforcement learning cover sequential choices under uncertainty, and numerical methods add root-finding, integration and approximation. These contributions do not combine into Maastricht’s sustained simplex, duality, flows and queueing sequence. UCR Econometrics adds OLS, GLS, instrumental variables and an empirical paper. Maastricht’s course explicitly includes dynamic models and time series and uses R and EViews. UCR statistics adds regression, inference and diagnostics; machine learning and neural networks contribute prediction rather than an equivalent econometric sequence. Introduction to Economics includes game theory, and Microeconomics & Behavior and Behavioral Economics give genuine but limited decision-making content relative to the specialist game-theory and information courses. The applied option adds market research through actual data collection and analysis, consumer engagement, banking and risk, bond, stock and derivative pricing, public economics, business AI and SQL. Market Research and Database Management Systems make concrete applied contributions within their official descriptions. The options share 17 courses and differ by seven courses each, with distinctly different organising questions. The remaining interests are either owned by these options or support-only or outcome rows. The broad option already represents optimisation, algorithms and quantitative research, so reshuffling those courses would not produce a third distinct direction.

alignment.rationale: Both study differentiation in one variable. Maastricht combines this with mathematical reasoning and sequences.
Linear Algebra covers matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations, the same subject as the target's Linear Algebra.
Both cover multivariable calculus and differential equations. Maastricht gives more attention to rigorous analysis and constrained optimisation.
Probability & Statistics teaches probability theory and distributions, the primary subject of Probability Theory; it adds estimation that belongs to Mathematical Statistics.
Both develop statistical inference and estimation. UCR focuses on applied experimental designs and regression, while Maastricht develops the mathematical theory.
Both study regression estimation, hypothesis testing and economic data. UCR includes instrumental variables and an empirical paper. Maastricht also teaches time-series models and uses R and EViews.
Introduction to Programming teaches Python programming and problem solving, the subject of the target's Programming component.
Both study linear programming and optimisation. UCR places these alongside search and constraint methods, while Maastricht teaches simplex methods, duality and nonlinear programming in greater depth.
Both study graph algorithms, including shortest paths and spanning trees. Maastricht also covers network flows, stochastic processes and queues.
Introduction to Economics covers game theory and market structure in its microeconomics part, an identifiable part of Game Theory and Economics; UCR has no dedicated game-theory course.
Microeconomics & Behavior covers consumer choice, market structures and strategic behaviour, the subject of Microeconomics at a more advanced level.
International Macroeconomics covers national income, growth, inflation and policy, the same subject as Macroeconomics.
Both study risk and return and price bonds and stocks. UCR also covers banking and derivatives. This course appears in the finance option.
The UCR options distribute relevant study between macroeconomics and finance. Maastricht combines exchange-rate modelling and international finance in one course.
Maastricht uses mathematical models for operations and marketing. UCR studies related tools across its research methods, optimisation and market courses.
UCR studies behavioural and computational approaches to uncertainty. Maastricht develops formal microeconomic models of risk and information.
Maastricht has a dedicated Philosophy of Science skills course.
Maastricht has a dedicated course on ethical, social and practical issues in econometrics.
Maastricht combines optimisation, game theory and programming in a team project with reports and a presentation.
Maastricht assesses a practical case integrating operations research and econometrics through a paper and presentation.
The comparator includes a required period at a partner university.
Students choose one of two disciplinary software courses. UCR provides general programming and data methods in separate courses.
Maastricht requires a supervised individual paper. UCR displays optional independent research alongside it.
One of two course choices from the four-course disciplinary list.
The second choice from the four-course disciplinary list. UCR offers related algorithms and deep learning in the mathematical option.
Students choose from the programme elective list.
